title: James–Stein as a named shrinkage surprise
dek: Wikipedia Stein paradox: for p≥3, shrinking MLEs toward a point can beat them in total MSE. Partial pooling is the hierarchical sequel.
story: James–Stein on Wikipedia is the surprise that for three or more Gaussian means, the vector of sample means is inadmissible under squared error: shrinking toward a point (or the grand mean) can cut total MSE. It looks like cheating. It is using extra structure.
stats-partial-pooling and stats-eight-schools are how a TB lab should actually shrink (hierarchies, not a 1961 formula pasted on MICs).
Cramér–Rao is not violated because James–Stein is biased (wiki-cramer-rao).
deep: p=1,2: the surprise does not fire in the same way.
You can increase MSE for one coordinate while cutting the sum — beware if that coordinate is 'the new drug'.
Empirical Bayes is the estimation-of-the-prior-view of the same shrinkage (next card).
Do not shrink a single pre-registered primary endpoint with Stein as perfume.

visual.caption: Unshrunk MLEs sit inside a larger decision problem where a shrinkage rule can dominate in total MSE when p≥3.
